docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Status: Current / Internal Detail Limited

This public documentation keeps implementation details high level.

ONSET3 includes a web application, server-side product logic, persistent product data and integrations with external identity and blockchain-related services.

Technical documentation can expand when public integration surfaces become real.

Potential future documentation areas include public APIs, embeds, webhooks, SDKs and integration guides.

No public API should be assumed merely because this Developers section exists.

docs.title: Calendar
docs.text:
Status: Current

The personal calendar organizes time-sensitive NFT activity.

Calendar entries can represent tracked launches and, as the product expands, relevant events and other scheduled actions.

The calendar is intended to answer a simple question:

What do I need to remember, and when?

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
Status: Current

Discovery is the entry point for finding relevant projects and launch activity.

The experience is designed around:

  • project discovery;
  • launch discovery;
  • search;
  • categories;
  • supported chains;
  • status filters;
  • launch timing;
  • verified information where available.

Discovery should remain useful without turning into an endless social feed.

docs.title: Launches
docs.text:
Status: Current

Launch pages are time-sensitive views associated with projects.

A launch can include:

  • launch date and time;
  • countdown;
  • chain;
  • price;
  • supply where relevant;
  • launch or mint stages;
  • allowlist information;
  • official external destination;
  • status such as upcoming, live or ended.

ONSET3 routes external mint actions to clearly identified official destinations rather than acting as a minting platform itself.

docs.title: My WL
docs.text:
Status: Current

My WL means: I have allowlist access.

This state is different from Watchlist because it represents access rather than general interest.

My WL can be used to organize the launches where the user has a specific action to remember.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
Status: Current / Expanding

Notifications support time-sensitive tracking.

Notification categories can include:

  • launch reminders;
  • allowlist reminders;
  • project updates;
  • launch-time changes;
  • event activity;
  • campaign updates.

Delivery channels may evolve independently. A documented notification type does not automatically mean every delivery channel is currently available.

docs.title: Discover & Track
docs.text:
Status: Current

Discovery and tracking form the core ONSET3 product foundation.

Users should be able to find a project or launch, understand the important information quickly, decide whether it matters to them, and save the relevant action without relying on scattered external notes.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
Status: Current

A Project Profile represents the persistent identity of a project.

The product structure can include:

  • project identity and description;
  • official links;
  • media;
  • key information;
  • item or collection preview;
  • launch information;
  • project roadmap;
  • verification state.

A Project is not duplicated for every launch or event. Those activities belong to the same project identity.

docs.title: Watchlist
docs.text:
Status: Current

Watchlist means: I am interested.

A user can save a project they want to monitor without claiming they have access to a launch.

Watchlist is intentionally separate from allowlist tracking.

docs.title: For Projects
docs.text:
Status: Current + Roadmap

ONSET3 gives projects a structured way to present official information and manage time-sensitive activity.

The project-side product includes project submission, launch information, project profile management, verification, dashboard workflows and future event/campaign management.

docs.title: Project Dashboard
docs.text:
Status: Current / Expanding

The Project Dashboard is the owner-facing workspace for project records.

It can surface drafts, submitted projects, review status, published projects, pending changes and project actions.

Future versions can extend the same workspace to Events, Campaigns and project-level analytics.

docs.title: Project Management
docs.text:
Status: Current / Expanding

Published projects should be maintainable without losing review history.

Material changes may require review again before replacing public information. The objective is to preserve both freshness and trust.

docs.title: Submit a Project
docs.text:
Status: Current

Project submission collects the information required to create and review a project presence on ONSET3.

The workflow can cover project information, launch information, blockchain details, mint details, schedule, official links, media, roadmap, preview and submission for review.

Submission status is separate from public publication status.

docs.title: Project Verification
docs.text:
Status: Current

Verification indicates that ONSET3 has reviewed specified project information or official destinations according to its verification process.

Verification is an informational state, not a generic endorsement badge.

Changes to important identity, destination or launch information can require re-verification.

docs.title: Chain Activity
docs.text:
Status: Future

Chain Activity compares NFT behavior across supported networks.

Potential views include NFT activity by chain, collector distribution, launch activity, transaction activity, volume, cross-chain behavior and changes in project deployment patterns.

Comparisons should account for differences in chain structure and available data.

docs.title: Collection & Project Signals
docs.text:
Status: Future

Collection and Project Signals translate measurable activity into structured context.

Potential signals include activity momentum, collector growth, holder changes, trading activity, launch interest, post-launch participation, concentration changes and repeat collector activity.

Signals should explain what changed and what data produced the signal.

docs.title: Collector Behavior
docs.text:
Status: Future

Collector Behavior focuses on aggregate patterns in how NFT participants act.

Potential areas include wallet activity patterns, mint participation, buying and selling behavior, holding duration, collection overlap, collector retention, new versus returning collectors, wallet segmentation and cross-chain participation.

Any use of user-linked data must have clear privacy boundaries and should favor aggregated analysis over exposure of individual behavior.

docs.title: Intelligence Reports
docs.text:
Status: Future

ONSET3 Intelligence can eventually produce structured recurring reports from the same underlying data layer.

Potential formats include Weekly NFT Market Report, Collector Behavior Report, Launch Performance Report, Chain Activity Report and Collection Intelligence Report.

Reports should be reproducible from measurable inputs and clearly distinguish data, interpretation and uncertainty.

docs.title: Launch Performance
docs.text:
Status: Future

Launch Performance analyzes behavior around a launch rather than treating the mint date as the end of the story.

Potential metrics include participation, sell-through, mint velocity, stage performance, collector acquisition, wallet concentration, post-mint activity and retention after launch.

docs.title: Market Signals
docs.text:
Status: Future

Market Signals are concise, data-derived indicators intended to make complex activity easier to understand.

Examples may include Rising Activity, Collector Accumulation, Increasing Participation, Declining Activity, High Wallet Concentration, New Collector Growth and Post-Launch Momentum.

These are information signals, not buy/sell signals.

Each signal should eventually expose its data basis, time window and limitations.

docs.title: Market Trends
docs.text:
Status: Future

Market Trends identify broader changes that persist beyond a single collection.

Potential categories include growing or declining sectors, changing collector behavior, emerging collections, launch format changes, chain migration, shifts in holding and trading behavior and broader NFT market cycles.

Trend reporting should separate measured change from interpretation.

docs.title: NFT Market Intelligence
docs.text:
Status: Future

NFT Market Intelligence is intended to describe measurable market conditions.

Potential inputs and outputs include market activity, volume trends, sales activity, liquidity indicators, active collections, chain distribution, category-level movement and changing market participation.

The objective is interpretation of market structure, not price prediction presented as certainty.

docs.title: ONSET3 Intelligence
docs.text:
Status: Future

ONSET3 Intelligence is the future data layer for understanding NFT markets, projects, launches and collector behavior.

The purpose is not to produce generic dashboards or speculative buy/sell calls. It is to convert measurable activity into useful context.

The intelligence layer covers NFT market intelligence, collector behavior, collection/project signals, launch performance, chain activity, market trends, market signals and intelligence reports.

docs.title: Campaigns
docs.text:
Status: Roadmap

Campaigns provide structured participation around a project.

A campaign can contain project, title and description, start/end dates, tasks, participant state and progress.

The first campaign layer does not assume financial custody, prize smart contracts, a token economy or a complex leaderboard.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Status: Roadmap

Events represent scheduled activities around a project or community.

Potential event types include:

  • mint;
  • reveal;
  • AMA;
  • X Space;
  • community call;
  • claim;
  • drop;
  • meetup;
  • conference;
  • tournament;
  • custom event.

The initial event model is intentionally lightweight: project, title, date/time, destination and calendar action.

docs.title: Participation Overview
docs.text:
Status: Roadmap

Participation extends ONSET3 beyond passive discovery.

The participation layer contains two primary concepts:

  • Events for scheduled activities;
  • Campaigns for structured task-based participation.

These features are designed to connect directly to existing project identities instead of creating a separate ecosystem.

docs.title: Activity
docs.text:
Status: Expansion

Portfolio Activity adds historical context to current holdings.

Planned categories include minted, bought, sold, received, sent and transfers.

Transaction classification must distinguish genuine purchases and sales from transfers, airdrops, self-transfers and other blockchain activity.

docs.title: Analytics
docs.text:
Status: Expansion

Portfolio Analytics is the most data-sensitive Portfolio phase.

Potential metrics include purchase cost, sales value, cost basis, current estimated value, realized profit/loss and unrealized profit/loss.

These metrics should only be shown when the underlying data supports a defensible calculation.

docs.title: Holdings
docs.text:
Status: Next

Holdings are the first Portfolio phase.

The goal is a clear visual inventory of NFTs owned, collections, chains, multiple added wallets, collection-level grouping and NFT-level items.

This phase prioritizes ownership visibility rather than financial performance calculations.

docs.title: Portfolio Overview
docs.text:
Status: Next

Portfolio brings a collector's NFT inventory into ONSET3 without changing the account system into wallet-based authentication.

The portfolio roadmap has three phases:

  1. Holdings — wallets, NFTs, collections and chain grouping.
  2. Activity — mint, buy, sell, receive and send history.
  3. Analytics — cost basis, realized/unrealized performance and valuation where reliable data exists.

Each phase should be useful independently.

docs.title: Wallets
docs.text:
Status: Next

The initial wallet model is address-based.

Users can add one or more wallet addresses to their ONSET3 account for portfolio visibility.

Wallet connection or signature-based ownership verification can be introduced later where it provides a clear product benefit.

docs.title: Core Product Principles
docs.text:
Status: Current

ONSET3 follows a small set of product rules:

  • Discovery first. Information should be useful before requiring deep interaction.
  • Time matters. Launches and events are time-sensitive and should be presented accordingly.
  • Project and event identity are separate. One project can have multiple launches and events.
  • Official destinations must be clear. External links should never be visually ambiguous.
  • Tracking should be personal. Interest, allowlist access and calendar intent are different states.
  • Verification is informational, not endorsement.
  • Roadmap features must not be presented as live.
  • Crypto complexity should not be added unless it improves the actual user task.

docs.title: How ONSET3 Works
docs.text:
Status: Current + Roadmap

A typical collector journey is:

Discover
  ↓
Project
  ↓
Launch or Event
  ↓
Watch / Track / Save
  ↓
Calendar or Reminder
  ↓
Participate
  ↓
Portfolio
  ↓
Intelligence

The early product is focused on the upper part of this flow. Portfolio, participation and intelligence expand the same journey rather than creating unrelated products.

docs.title: Product Overview
docs.text:
Status: Current

ONSET3 is organized around five product actions:

  • Discover relevant NFT projects and launches.
  • Track personal interest, access and time-sensitive activity.
  • Participate in events and campaigns.
  • Manage project presence and submissions.
  • Verify official information and destinations.

The product is designed to grow without collapsing every concept into one feed. Projects, launches, events, campaigns, wallets and portfolio data are separate entities with different purposes.

docs.title: Product Entities
docs.text:
Status: Current + Roadmap

ONSET3 uses distinct entities so information remains structured.

docs.title: Project
docs.text: The persistent identity of a project.

docs.title: Launch
docs.text: A time-based launch, mint, claim or release associated with a project.

docs.title: Event
docs.text: A scheduled activity associated with a project or community.

docs.title: Campaign
docs.text: A structured participation experience containing tasks and progress.

docs.title: User
docs.text: An ONSET3 account used for personal tracking and project management.

docs.title: Wallet
docs.text: A blockchain address added for portfolio visibility.

docs.title: Portfolio
docs.text: An aggregated view of NFT holdings and later activity/analytics.

docs.title: Intelligence Signal
docs.text: A future derived market or behavior signal based on measurable data.

docs.title: Project vs Launch vs Event vs Campaign
docs.text:
Status: Current + Roadmap

These concepts are intentionally separate.

Entity Purpose Project Persistent project identity Launch Time-based release or mint activity Event Scheduled project/community activity Campaign Structured user participation with tasks

A single project can therefore contain multiple launches, multiple events and multiple campaigns over time.

This prevents ONSET3 from creating duplicate project profiles every time something new happens.

docs.title: Brand Assets
docs.text:
Status: Current

Brand: ONSET3 Tagline: Discover What's Next in NFTs.

Public brand assets can be added here as a controlled press and partner resource.

This page should eventually include approved logos, wordmarks, usage guidance and downloadable media once those assets are finalized.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Status: Current

docs.title: Is ONSET3 an NFT marketplace?
docs.text: No. The core product is focused on discovery, tracking, participation, portfolio visibility and future intelligence.

docs.title: Does verification mean a project is safe?
docs.text: No. Verification describes reviewed information within a defined scope. It is not an endorsement or financial guarantee.

docs.title: Is Portfolio live?
docs.text: Portfolio is documented as a next-stage product layer unless its status is updated on the Portfolio pages.

docs.title: Are Campaigns financial reward systems?
docs.text: The initial Campaign direction is task-based participation without assuming financial custody, prize smart contracts or a token economy.

docs.title: Does ONSET3 provide investment advice?
docs.text: No. Market and intelligence features are intended to provide data and context, not individualized investment advice.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Status: Current

Allowlist / WL — Access granted to a specific launch stage.

Watchlist — A personal state meaning the user is interested in a project.

My WL — A personal state meaning the user has allowlist access.

Project — The persistent identity of a project on ONSET3.

Launch — A time-based mint, release, claim or related launch activity.

Event — A scheduled project or community activity.

Campaign — Structured participation containing tasks and progress.

GTD — Guaranteed allocation stage.

FCFS — First come, first served stage.

Public — Publicly available launch stage.

Reveal — Publication of previously hidden collection information or media.

Claim — A time-based action allowing eligible users to receive an asset or benefit.

Verified Project — A project whose specified information has been reviewed by ONSET3.

Onchain Verified — A separate verification state based on supported blockchain information.

Signal — A future data-derived indicator describing measurable market or behavior change.

docs.title: Report an Issue
docs.text:
Status: Current

Incorrect project information, broken official links, suspicious destinations and documentation errors should be reportable through a clear ONSET3 support path.

Until a dedicated reporting workflow is documented here, users should avoid relying on uncertain information and verify sensitive actions directly through official project channels.

docs.title: Roadmap Overview
docs.text:
Status: Living Document

The ONSET3 roadmap is organized by product maturity rather than speculative quarterly dates.

The four roadmap layers are Current, Next, Expansion and Future.

This structure makes it clear what is part of the product today and what remains directional.

docs.title: Current Product Status
docs.text:
Status: Living Document

ONSET3 separates documentation by product maturity.

Status Meaning Current Part of the active product foundation Beta Available but still being refined Next Near-term product work Roadmap Approved direction, not yet a current capability Future Longer-term product concept

The current product foundation is centered on project and launch discovery, project profiles, launch information, tracking, project submission and verification workflows.

Portfolio, Events, Campaigns and ONSET3 Intelligence are documented as roadmap layers and must not be interpreted as fully live capabilities unless their individual page status changes.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text:
Status: Product Direction

ONSET3 aims to become an operating layer for the NFT ecosystem.

The product direction follows four stages:

  1. Discover — find projects, launches and relevant activity.
  2. Track — organize watchlists, allowlists, launch dates and reminders.
  3. Participate — join events and campaigns around projects.
  4. Understand — use portfolio and intelligence tools to understand personal activity, collector behavior and the broader NFT market.

The goal is not to add every possible Web3 feature. Each layer should make NFT discovery and decision-making clearer.

docs.title: What is ONSET3?
docs.text:
Status: Current

ONSET3 is a product layer for discovering NFT projects and launches, tracking the opportunities that matter to a collector, and organizing time-sensitive actions such as allowlists and launch dates.

Its broader product direction extends this foundation into participation tools, NFT portfolio visibility and market intelligence.

ONSET3 is not intended to be another NFT marketplace. The product focuses on helping users understand what is happening, when it is happening, where the official destination is, and what they personally need to track.

docs.title: Why ONSET3?
docs.text:
Status: Current

NFT discovery is fragmented across social feeds, project websites, community servers, marketplaces and private bookmarks.

This creates recurring problems:

  • launches are easy to miss;
  • allowlist access is difficult to organize;
  • project information is scattered;
  • official destinations can be unclear;
  • collectors often rely on screenshots, bookmarks and multiple calendars;
  • useful market context is separated from the actions collectors actually take.

ONSET3 is designed to reduce that fragmentation by combining discovery, tracking, participation and eventually intelligence in one product.

docs.title: Official Information
docs.text:
Status: Current

Official information can include project website, X account, community destination, contract information, mint destination, marketplace destination and other project-controlled links.

External destinations should be labeled clearly.

docs.title: Trust Overview
docs.text:
Status: Current

Trust is a product layer in ONSET3.

The system focuses on clearly identified official information, verification states, external destination clarity, change history and user-facing safety context.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
Status: Current

Users should independently verify sensitive actions before signing transactions or sending funds.

ONSET3 can reduce ambiguity by identifying reviewed information and official destinations, but external sites, contracts, wallets and third-party services remain outside ONSET3's direct control.

docs.title: Verification Limitations
docs.text:
Status: Current

Verification does not mean endorsement.

A verified project is not automatically a safe investment, technically secure, free from contract risk, guaranteed to launch successfully, guaranteed to retain value or recommended by ONSET3.

Verification communicates the scope of information ONSET3 has reviewed.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Status: Current

ONSET3 can distinguish multiple information states, including Unverified, Verified Project and Onchain Verified where supported by a separate onchain verification process.

Verification levels should not be collapsed into one generic badge.
